stories.title: How to preapply for home repair help in Detroit
stories.summary: Residents can check their eligibility and add their name to the list for home repair assistance through Sept. 22.

photo.alt: Abandoned house in Detroit neighborhoods

stories.title: As enrollments plummet, Michigan communities sweat job losses from universities
stories.summary: Michigan's public universities are facing significant enrollment declines, which are expected to have adverse economic effects on communities across the state. The state's 15 public universities employ 97,000 faculty and staff, and the economic impact of these institutions is substantial, but the combination of declining enrollments and limited state aid is putting financial pressure on the schools.

photo.alt: Mount Pleasant, Michigan

stories.title: Spending the Golden Years in Treetown
stories.summary: Tracey Lind and Emily Ingalls chose Ann Arbor for retirement due to its affordability, cultural richness, and welcoming community. The city has been recognized as one of the best places to retire in the U.S.

photo.alt: Tracey Lind and Emily Ingalls in Ann Arbor

stories.title: U.S. Supreme Court ruled against Trump . . . for now
stories.summary: The U.S. Supreme Court has upheld a preliminary injunction blocking the U.S. Postal Service (USPS) from implementing new mail-in ballot requirements. The ruling leaves the current election procedures in place, but Justice Kavanaugh noted that such changes could be within USPS jurisdiction if implemented with sufficient time before elections.

source.name: Kalloli Bhatt, Zoe Clark, Rick Pluta

photo.alt: Election newsletter graphic

stories.title: MichMash: Top 10 Michigan House seats that could flip in the 2026 midterms
stories.summary: WDET’s weekly series discusses 10 Michigan House races that could change party control in the 2026 midterms. The national political environment and local politicians' records are key factors.

photo.alt: Screenshot of MichMash podcast episode

stories.title: A Millage to Keep Metro Detroit's Stories Alive
stories.summary: A proposed millage in Wayne and Oakland counties aims to support the Detroit Historical Society and the Charles H. Wright Museum of African American History, providing free admission, transportation assistance, and funding for smaller museums. The measure, listed as the Southeast Michigan Historical Museums Authority proposal, is set for the November 3 ballot.

photo.alt: Detroit Historical Society and Charles H. Wright Museum of African American History

stories.title: Eastbound I-94 in Wayne County closed for jackknifed semi-truck
stories.summary: Eastbound I-94 is closed at Michigan Avenue in Dearborn after a semi-trailer truck jackknifed, according to state police.

photo.alt: Jackknifed semi-truck on I-94

stories.title: Proposed repeal of ‘Roadless Rule’ could open Michigan national forests to logging, roadbuilding
stories.summary: The U.S. Forest Service has proposed to rescind the 2001 Roadless Area Conservation Rule, which could open about 16,000 acres of protected national forest land in Michigan to road construction and logging. Environmental advocates argue that this could increase the risk of wildfires and harm wildlife habitats.

photo.alt: Overlook from the Trap Hills within the Ottawa National Forest

stories.title: The Metro: An initiative wants to remove money from Michigan politics. Can it?
stories.summary: A local campaign in Michigan, Michiganders for Money Out of Politics, is pushing a ballot measure to limit political spending by big-time actors, aiming to reduce corruption. The measure will be voted on in the November 3 election, despite opposition seeking to block it.
topics: michiganders for money out of politics

photo.alt: Voting booths

stories.title: Consumers Energy asks state regulators to delay decision on hydroelectric dam sale until November
stories.summary: Consumers Energy has requested a 60-day extension from the Michigan Public Service Commission to delay the decision on the sale of 13 hydroelectric dams. The company believes this will allow time to address concerns raised during the proceedings.

photo.alt: Foote Dam in Iosco County, one of 13 hydroelectric dams proposed for sale by Consumers Energy.

stories.title: Commissioners greenlight natural gas rate increase, improved outage credits
stories.summary: The Michigan Public Service Commission approved a $74.52 million natural gas rate increase for DTE Energy to modernize its gas system. They also approved a virtual power plant program and increased power outage credits for consumers.

photo.alt: Commissioners greenlight natural gas rate increase, improved outage credits

stories.title: Hytek and Freshy Fine bring award-winning Lantz to new vapes
stories.summary: Detroit cultivator Hytek and Michigan cannabis brand Freshy Fine have collaborated to release a disposable vape featuring Lantz, an award-winning cannabis strain. The product will be available at various dispensaries starting Friday, September 18, 2026.

photo.alt: Hytek x Freshy Fine Vape Teaser

stories.title: Trump Administration Rolls Back Power Plant Emissions Rules
stories.summary: The Trump administration announced it will roll back rules governing power plant emissions, despite evidence of climate change and scientific consensus on human causation. Rachel Rothschild, an assistant professor at Michigan Law, discusses the implications.

photo.alt: Stateside Full Show Pod

stories.title: The Dish Explores Traverse City's Food Scene
stories.summary: The Dish, a segment on Stateside, takes a long weekend Up North to explore Traverse City's unique food scene with top chefs, highlighting what makes it special.

photo.alt: Stateside Full Show Pod

stories.title: Lillian Li Discusses Her Novel 'Bad Asians'
stories.summary: Author Lillian Li talks about her novel 'Bad Asians,' which explores the lives of high-achieving individuals coming of age during the Great Recession.

photo.alt: Stateside Full Show Pod

stories.title: Anti-ICE coalition asks Slotkin to help end ICE use of county jails for detention in Michigan
stories.summary: A coalition of Michigan-based organizations has sent a letter to U.S. Sen. Elissa Slotkin, urging her to help end the use of county jails as detention centers for ICE. The letter requests a congressional oversight visit, the release of withheld records, and support for a law banning the practice.

photo.alt: Melody Simmons, chair of the Coalition to Shut the Camps, speaks at a protest.

stories.title: Unless a buyer steps up, the Toledo Blade to print last edition at the end of the year
stories.summary: The Toledo Blade, a nearly 200-year-old newspaper in Northwest Ohio, will print its final edition at the end of the year unless a buyer is found. The decision was made due to unsustainable financial losses, as announced by Block Communications, the paper’s owner since 1925.

source.name: Beenish Ahmed, The Associated Press, Stateside Staff

photo.alt: A delivery van for the Toledo Blade parked in a lot.

stories.title: Michelin Guide to Host Great Lakes Ceremony in Detroit
stories.summary: The Michelin Guide is set to bring its Great Lakes ceremony to Detroit next April, marking a significant moment for the city's food scene. The event is expected to attract attention and tourism, with the potential for local restaurants to earn prestigious Michelin stars.

photo.alt: Newspaper opening cover

stories.title: Cass Cafe to Reopen in Detroit
stories.summary: Cass Cafe, a beloved Detroit institution, is set to reopen under the Chalfonte Foundation, a non-profit organization. The new Cass Cafe will feature a full bar, community space, and a focus on nutritious food, aiming to reconnect with the city's cultural roots.

photo.alt: Newspaper opening cover

stories.title: Highgrade Deli to Reopen in Detroit
stories.summary: Highgrade Deli, a long-standing Detroit establishment, is set to reopen this fall. The new owners, who purchased the deli from receivership, plan to bring back the beloved elements of the original while ensuring the space remains a vibrant part of the community.

photo.alt: Newspaper opening cover

stories.title: Agnes to Open in West Village
stories.summary: Agnes, a new restaurant from the team behind Selden Standard, is set to open in West Village. The restaurant will occupy the former Metropolitan Pizza Kitchen space and is expected to become a neighborhood favorite, offering a blend of upscale dining and community atmosphere.

photo.alt: Newspaper opening cover

stories.title: Aurora Italiana to Open in Downtown Detroit
stories.summary: Aurora Italiana, a colorful and upscale Italian restaurant, is expanding to downtown Detroit. The restaurant, known for its vibrant atmosphere and high-quality cuisine, will join the existing locations in Oakland County and bring a new dining option to the city.

photo.alt: Newspaper opening cover

stories.title: Slutty Vegan to Open in Michigan Central
stories.summary: Slutty Vegan, a popular vegan restaurant chain, is set to open in Michigan Central. Known for its colorful and playful vibe, the restaurant will offer a variety of vegan comfort food, adding to the growing dining scene in the area.

photo.alt: Newspaper opening cover

stories.title: Mike's Red Tacos to Open in Royal Oak
stories.summary: Mike's Red Tacos, a casual chain known for its beefy birria tacos, is set to open its first Michigan location in Royal Oak. The restaurant plans to expand to 15 locations across the state, bringing a new dining option to the area.

photo.alt: Newspaper opening cover

stories.title: Spiedo to Open on West Canfield
stories.summary: Spiedo, a new restaurant from Chef Brad Greenhill, is set to open on West Canfield, replacing the former Jolly Pumpkin location. The restaurant will offer Mediterranean and Middle Eastern-inspired cuisine, featuring grilled vegetables and meats, and a sit-down dining experience.

photo.alt: Newspaper opening cover

stories.title: Advocates, moms and lawmakers push for group prenatal care as Legislature weighs insurer issues
stories.summary: Sen. Stephanie Chang and other advocates are pushing for insurance coverage of group prenatal care in Michigan, highlighting its benefits for maternal and infant health. The Centering Pregnancy program, which provides group prenatal care, has seen increased adoption in the state, with 39 licensed sites.

photo.alt: Sen. Stephanie Chang speaking at an event in Lansing.

stories.title: New ‘Kids Count’ data shows drop in college readiness, education participation among young adults
stories.summary: The Michigan League for Public Policy released a report showing a decline in college readiness and education participation among young adults in Michigan, with the state ranking low in economic wellbeing and education. The report also highlights issues such as poverty, food insecurity, and reduced enrollment in social safety net programs.

photo.alt: Arabia Simeon, founder and CEO of Politics on the Go, discusses youth voter turnout at a panel discussion.

stories.title: A constitutional convention to limit abortion rights? Democrats push back on DeBoyer suggestion
stories.summary: Michigan Republican Rep. Jay DeBoyer proposed the idea of using a constitutional convention to reintroduce limits on abortion in Michigan, facing backlash from Democrats and reproductive rights groups. The suggestion was met with criticism, with opponents emphasizing the settled nature of abortion rights in the state and the potential dangers of such restrictions.

photo.alt: Screenshot of Rep. Jay DeBoyer speaking

stories.title: Hundreds of people may be denied Flint settlement money due to paperwork errors
stories.summary: Due to missing Social Security numbers or required signatures, hundreds of Flint water settlement claimants may lose their eligibility. A federal judge has authorized final notices to be sent, giving claimants 30 days to provide the missing information.

photo.alt: Flint Water Crisis

stories.title: City inspectors survey tornado damage
stories.summary: Detroit city inspectors have assessed the damage from a tornado that hit the east side and Belle Isle on September 3, affecting over 100 homes and businesses. Nine buildings need emergency demolition, and Mayor Mary Sheffield has declared a local state of emergency to seek disaster relief.

photo.alt: Tornado Damage in Detroit

stories.title: Michigan sees record high diesel fuel prices
stories.summary: The average cost of diesel fuel in Michigan has reached a record high of $6.26 per gallon, surpassing the previous record of $6.20 set in May. Gasoline prices have also risen, with an average increase of 12 cents per gallon from the previous day.

photo.alt: Fuel Prices in Michigan

stories.title: Michigan asks nonprofits to supplement SNAP after cuts
stories.summary: The state of Michigan is urging nonprofits to assist residents affected by federal cuts to the Supplemental Nutrition Assistance Program (SNAP) and Medicaid, which will take effect in January 2027. The state has allocated over $12 million to support these efforts until September 2028.

photo.alt: SNAP and Medicaid Cuts

stories.title: Benson, James pitch tariff remedies, business boosts & data center limits at Detroit Economic Club
stories.summary: Democratic gubernatorial nominee Jocelyn Benson and Republican nominee John James presented their economic plans at the Detroit Economic Club, focusing on tariff impacts, business growth, and data center regulations. Benson proposed negotiating subnational agreements with Canada, while James introduced a bill to use tariff revenue to offset costs.

photo.alt: Democratic gubernatorial nominee Secretary of State Jocelyn Benson speaks to the Detroit Economic Club.

stories.title: Detroit predicts revenue increase for 2027 budget
stories.summary: Detroit officials are estimating an increase of $58 million or more in revenue for the 2027 fiscal year, primarily due to increased corporate income, property, and wagering taxes. The city expects to start the next fiscal year with a $1.5 billion general fund.

photo.alt: Downtown Detroit skyline

stories.title: Sen. Gary Peters comments on SCOTUS absentee ballot ruling
stories.summary: The U.S. Supreme Court ruled against the Trump Administration's attempt to change mail-in ballot rules for the upcoming midterm elections. Sen. Gary Peters, a Democrat, is concerned about potential election interference by the Trump administration.

photo.alt: Downtown Detroit skyline

stories.title: Americans for Citizen Voting proposal won’t make ballot
stories.summary: The Board of State Canvassers deadlocked on the Americans for Citizen Voting proposal, preventing it from appearing on the ballot. The proposal aimed to require all voters to prove they are U.S. citizens. A State House Select Committee is investigating the issues with petition signatures.

photo.alt: Downtown Detroit skyline

stories.title: Health officials warn about recreational nitrous-oxide use
stories.summary: Michigan health officials are warning about the growing problem of recreational nitrous oxide use, which has led to a rise in hospitalizations and injuries. Since 2024, a third of emergency nitrous oxide cases in Michigan have required hospitalization.

photo.alt: Downtown Detroit skyline

stories.title: Gas prices rise
stories.summary: Fuel prices in Michigan are rising, with the average cost of regular unleaded gasoline increasing to $4.54 per gallon, up 11 cents from the previous day and 32 cents from a week ago. Diesel fuel is averaging a record $6.34 per gallon statewide.

photo.alt: Downtown Detroit skyline

stories.title: ‘Facts first, conclusions second’: House committee begins review of ballot measure procedures
stories.summary: Rep. Mike Harris (R-Waterford Township) chairs a new House Select Committee to examine the sampling procedures used by the Board of State Canvassers and Bureau of Elections for verifying signatures on ballot initiatives. The committee aims to ensure the process is fair and transparent, without prejudging the outcomes or political implications of specific measures.

photo.alt: Photo by Katherine Dailey/Michigan Advance

stories.title: South Lyon City Council directs staff to examine impacts of canceling Flock contract
stories.summary: The South Lyon City Council has directed its staff to examine the legal and financial impacts of canceling the contracts for Flock license plate reader cameras. The decision comes after community concerns over privacy and potential misuse of the technology.

photo.alt: Flock license plate reader camera in South Lyon

stories.title: Michigan Border Crossings Close to Commemorate 9/11
stories.summary: All international border crossings in Michigan were briefly closed to commemorate the 25th anniversary of the Sept. 11 terrorist attacks, which killed nearly 3000 people, including at least 42 with ties to Michigan.

photo.alt: 9-11 memorial image

stories.title: Lochmoor Club Destroyed by Fire
stories.summary: The historic Lochmoor Club in Grosse Pointe Woods, built in 1969, was destroyed by a fire that started in the kitchen on Sept. 9. Local officials have declared it a total loss, and the school district warns of poor air quality nearby.

photo.alt: Lochmoor Club Destroyed by Fire

stories.title: Detroit Lions to Face New Orleans Saints in Season Opener
stories.summary: The Detroit Lions will kick off their 2026 NFL season at home against the New Orleans Saints on Sunday at 1:00 p.m. EST.

photo.alt: Detroit Lions to Face New Orleans Saints in Season Opener

stories.title: Tigers to Play Rockies in Weekend Series
stories.summary: The Detroit Tigers will play a weekend series against the Colorado Rockies. The Tigers are currently second to last in the American League Central with a 67-79 record.

photo.alt: Tigers to Play Rockies in Weekend Series

stories.title: Detroit City FC to Play in Sacramento
stories.summary: Detroit City FC will play against Sacramento Republic FC in Heart Health Park, Sacramento, California, with the game starting at 10:00 p.m. EST.

photo.alt: Detroit City FC to Play in Sacramento

stories.title: National Black Footwear Forum in Detroit
stories.summary: The 2026 National Black Footwear Forum is taking place this weekend at the Pensole Lewis College of Business and Design in Detroit, highlighting the collective power of Black leaders in the footwear industry.

photo.alt: National Black Footwear Forum in Detroit

stories.title: WDET staff reflect on 9/11 and lessons learned on 25th anniversary
stories.summary: WDET newsroom and staff from The Metro share their personal experiences and reflections on the 25th anniversary of the September 11th attacks, highlighting where they were and how the events have impacted them.

photo.alt: A reflective image related to the 9/11 anniversary

stories.title: Environmentalists push lawmakers to forge ahead on moratorium and regulations for data centers
stories.summary: Environmental groups are urging Michigan lawmakers to implement a moratorium and establish regulations for data center developments, citing concerns over environmental and community impacts. The push comes as legislative proposals remain stalled in committees.

photo.alt: A server room in a data center

stories.title: The Metro: The government tried to erase her family. She found their names
stories.summary: Sierra Biidaaban Nadeau, the Traverse City Record-Eagle’s first full-time Native American reporter, uncovered 10 of her relatives in the enrollment records of Michigan's Native American boarding schools, including her great-grandfather and his siblings. Her findings, documented in 'What the Ancestors Say,' reveal the impact of these institutions on her family and the broader Native American community.

photo.alt: Sierra Biidaaban Nadeau, Native American journalist

stories.title: Michigan State Police removes tens of thousands from sex offender registry after court order
stories.summary: The Michigan State Police have begun removing individuals from the state’s sex offender registry following a Michigan Supreme Court ruling that the 2021 amendments to the Sex Offender Registration Act could not retroactively extend registration requirements to crimes committed before July 1, 2011.

photo.alt: Michigan State Police logo

stories.title: Why Michigan Has the Most to Lose in a U.S. - Canada Trade War
stories.summary: Michigan faces significant economic impacts from a sudden U.S.-Canada trade war, affecting auto supply chains, materials, local jobs, healthcare workers, and tourism. Glenn Stevens from MICHAuto discusses the implications and the importance of resolving the dispute.

photo.alt: Drone view of the Detroit River and surrounding areas

stories.title: A Data Center on the Huron River: Ypsilanti Township Pushes Back
stories.summary: Ypsilanti Township residents and officials are pushing back against the University of Michigan and Los Alamos National Laboratory's plan to build a $1.25 billion research computing center on a 144-acre site along the Huron River. Concerns include environmental impact, water use, and community engagement.

source.name: Sadie Jacobson, Alice VanderVliet, Alden Koschmann, Caroline Mathern, Roshan Malani, Lucas Oorbeck, Mia Benjey, and Adam Cameron
source.publication: The Communicator (Ann Arbor Community High School)

stories.title: NCAA Offers No Relief for Western Michigan After Last-Second Loss to Michigan
stories.summary: The NCAA has announced that Michigan's football team should not have been given an extra second that allowed it to beat Western Michigan on a Hail Mary pass. However, there is no mechanism to overturn the game's result.

photo.alt: Big Ten football game

stories.title: Michigan State Faces Notre Dame in Tough Road Game
stories.summary: Michigan State's unranked Spartans will face No. 3 Notre Dame on the road. Head coach Pat Fitzgerald emphasizes the importance of strong defense to give the offense a chance in this challenging game.

photo.alt: Michigan State Faces Notre Dame in Tough Road Game

stories.title: Michigan Prepares for UTEP with Heavy Favorite Status
stories.summary: Michigan, coming off a win against Oklahoma, is a heavy favorite against UTEP. The game provides an opportunity for the Wolverines to work on their offense before Big Ten conference play.

photo.alt: Michigan Prepares for UTEP with Heavy Favorite Status

stories.title: Detroit Red Wings in Disarray After GM Changes and Captain's Departure
stories.summary: The Detroit Red Wings are facing organizational turmoil with the departure of GM Steve Yzerman, the removal of captain Dylan Larkin's 'C', and the appointment of Shawn Horcoff as interim GM.

photo.alt: Detroit Red Wings in Disarray After GM Changes and Captain's Departure

stories.title: Contract dispute: clubs look toward a return to normal
stories.summary: Since the start of 2026, Ann Arbor Public Schools teachers have worked without a contract, leading to the suspension of after-school clubs. With a tentative agreement now reached, students and teachers are preparing for a return to normal extracurricular activities, though the impact of the dispute is expected to linger.

source.name: Amy Yang and Ishaan Kamat
source.publication: The Huron Emery (Ann Arbor Huron High School)

stories.title: The Metro: Can Detroiters heal without waiting on the system?
stories.summary: A community project called the Healing Hub in Detroit provides a safe space for kids and free food to those in need. Detroit Heals Detroit, which started as a high school writing project, aims to expand its free grocery store pop-ups across the city.

photo.alt: Sirrita Darby, co-founder of Detroit Heals Detroit

stories.title: School year starts off strong with Fall Picture Day and class meetings
stories.summary: On September 1, Huron High School held its annual Fall Picture Day for ID and yearbook photos, followed by grade-level class meetings to build community and set expectations for the school year.

source.name: Lakshya Jaiganesh, Website Editor-In-Chief
source.publication: The Huron Emery (Ann Arbor Huron High School)

stories.title: From Community to College and Back Again
stories.summary: CHS senior Violet Selcer and senior Mark Ionides are taking University of Michigan courses this year, either through the Community Resource (CR) program or dual enrollment. These opportunities allow high school students to challenge themselves with college-level courses and gain early exposure to university life.

source.name: Eli Feng, Luke Gery, and Caitlinn Cho
source.publication: The Communicator (Ann Arbor Community High School)

stories.title: Day of Reckoning Nears for AAPS
stories.summary: Ann Arbor Public Schools is considering closing several schools, including Pittsfield Elementary and Pathways alternative high school, to address financial issues and declining enrollment. The decision is expected to be made in the next few months, with the potential for significant community opposition.

photo.alt: Pittsfield Elementary School

stories.title: DOJ demands Ann Arbor Public Schools change transgender student policy
stories.summary: The U.S. Department of Justice has demanded that Ann Arbor Public Schools revise or rescind its policy on transgender and gender nonconforming students, claiming it violates federal laws by preventing parents from accessing their children’s records. The district faces the risk of losing $15 million in federal funding if it does not comply within 14 days.

photo.alt: Ann Arbor Public Schools building

stories.title: Melodies Frozen in Time as Skyline High School Leaves Its Mark At Interlochen
stories.summary: Skyline High School's performing arts program participates in an annual event at Interlochen, where students from various ensembles rehearse and perform, fostering a strong sense of community and musical growth.

source.name: Della Bank
source.publication: The Communicator (Ann Arbor Community High School)

photo.alt: Students at Skyline High School performing arts program at Interlochen

stories.title: Michigan rabbis push El-Sayed to change rhetoric on Israel, ensure safety of Jewish community
stories.summary: A new coalition of Jewish clergy and synagogue leaders in Michigan, Nonnegotiable Michigan, has called on Democratic U.S. Senate nominee Abdul El-Sayed to affirm community needs, including Jewish safety and respect for Jewish identities, as the community feels threatened by his rhetoric on Israel. El-Sayed is working to mend ties with the Jewish community through meetings and conversations with leaders.

photo.alt: Abdul El-Sayed at an election night watch party in Detroit, Mich., on Aug. 4, 2026

stories.title: Big House advertisements draw mixed reactions from Michigan fans
stories.summary: For the first time in its 99-year history, Michigan Stadium is displaying advertisements as part of the new Leaders and Best Champion Partners Program, aimed at raising revenue to support student-athlete contracts. The ads, featuring Coca-Cola, Meijer, and Google Gemini, have received mixed reactions from fans and alumni, with some supporting the move and others concerned about the promotion of AI companies.

photo.alt: Michigan Stadium with advertisements

stories.title: Will Lawrence rolls out plan for regulating Big Tech, data centers in Michigan and beyond
stories.summary: Democratic nominee William Lawrence has unveiled a plan to regulate data centers and AI development, aiming to protect communities and jobs. The plan includes a federal moratorium on data center development and a national AI compact with environmental, safety, and job protection measures.

photo.alt: William Lawrence speaking at a rally

stories.title: Michigan Science Center Launches New Weekend Dissection Program: “insides Out” Presented by Medline
stories.summary: The Michigan Science Center has introduced a new educational program called 'insides Out', presented by Medline Inc., aimed at children and families to enhance their understanding of anatomy and health.

stories.title: Northside Grill owner battles city over 20 inches of land
stories.summary: Jim Koli, the owner of Northside Grill and other historic buildings in Ann Arbor, is in a legal dispute with the city over 20 inches of land his buildings encroach upon. The issue has led to $78,000 in legal fees and remains unresolved, with Koli seeking a permanent easement.

photo.alt: Northside Grill and historic buildings on Broadway Street

stories.title: Cristine Mary (Hall) (Ross) Gray
stories.summary: Cristine Mary (Hall) (Ross) Gray, a dedicated occupational therapist and loving mother, passed away on July 6, 2026. She was known for her work with young adults with disabilities and her passion for papercrafting during retirement.

photo.alt: Cristine Mary (Hall) (Ross) Gray

stories.title: How the American revolt against Flock cameras mirrors the Boston Tea Party of 1773
stories.summary: A grassroots movement against automated license plate readers (ALPRs) has gained momentum, with parallels drawn to the American Revolution. Cities are revoking contracts with ALPR manufacturers, and citizens are taking direct action against the cameras, similar to colonial resistance against British rule.

photo.alt: A Flock license plate reader camera in Southfield

stories.title: Michigan State Police Encourage Installation of Tornado Saferooms
stories.summary: The Michigan State Police are promoting the installation of Tornado Saferooms and are considering a new rebate program to assist residents. Aarti Pradhan from 88.1 the Park interviewed Public Information Officer Clayton Cummins on the topic.

stories.title: Ann Arbor teachers rally before Board of Education meeting
stories.summary: Over 1500 teachers, students, and community members rallied outside the Earhart Administration Building on June 3, 2026, to support Ann Arbor Public Schools teachers working without a contract. The rally highlighted issues such as salary compensation, healthcare cost sharing, and the preservation of elementary enrichment classes.

source.name: Mia Lin, Staff Writer
source.publication: The Huron Emery (Ann Arbor Huron High School)

photo.alt: A young girl holds up a handmade sign supporting teachers at the rally.

stories.title: AAPS’ Tug-of-War Game of Negotiations: The Rope is Fraying
stories.summary: The article discusses the ongoing contract negotiations between Ann Arbor Public Schools (AAPS) and the Ann Arbor Educator Association (AAEA), highlighting the impact of work-to-rule actions by teachers and the broader implications for students and the community.

source.name: Eda Kirca, Natalie Hannewald, and The Skyline Post Editorial Board
source.publication: The Skyline Post (Ann Arbor Skyline High School)

stories.title: Plymouth DDA Plans 40-Million Dollar Streetscape Update
stories.summary: The City of Plymouth’s Downtown Development Authority is set to undertake a significant 40-million dollar update to the city’s streetscape. Director Sam Plymale discussed the project with 88.1 the Park’s Aarti Pradhan.

stories.title: Women’s Sports Spotlight – June 1, 2026
stories.summary: This month’s Women’s Sports Spotlight focuses on the soccer teams at Canton, Plymouth, and Salem High School, featuring interviews with players from each team.

stories.title: Summit on the Park Undergoes Major Renovation
stories.summary: The Summit on the Park in Canton is set for a major renovation. Facility Manager Jason Lombardo discussed the planned improvements and their impact on the community with 88.1 the Park’s Mahika Srivastava.

stories.title: Michigan Science Center Offers Free Summer Admission for Detroit First Responders and Their Families
stories.summary: The Michigan Science Center (Mi-Sci) has launched the 'Science of Safety,' a new summer initiative sponsored by Bank of America, which provides free admission to Detroit first responders and their families. The program explores the STEM behind firefighting, emergency medicine, and public safety technology as part of the America 250 celebration.

stories.title: Carrying the closet: The comeback of thrifting
stories.summary: Thrift stores have seen a significant rise in popularity, with the market value of thrifting growing to $61 billion in 2026. Campaigns like Oxfam's Second Hand September and economic factors such as inflation have contributed to this trend, alongside the appeal of unique finds and sustainability.

photo.alt: Clothes arranged in order by the colors of the rainbow at Plato’s Closet

stories.title: Zaman International's Work in Breaking the Cycle of Poverty
stories.summary: 88.1 the Park’s Alyssa Ajai interviewed Sarah deVeer, Zaman International’s Associate Director of Community Engagement and Outreach, discussing their mission to help women and children escape poverty in Southeast Michigan and beyond.

stories.title: Unified Sports Bocce Ball brings connection, confidence to P-CEP athletes
stories.summary: Unified Sports, a branch of the Special Olympics, organizes bocce ball matches and other sports for high school special education students, fostering connections and boosting confidence. The program adapts sports to meet the needs of participants, promoting teamwork and social skills.

photo.alt: P-CEP Unified athletes look over their bocce ball throws at Churchill match in Livonia.

stories.title: As 3D printing expands in schools, questions over intellectual property rise
stories.summary: 3D printing technology has become increasingly accessible in schools, allowing students to create physical objects from digital designs. However, this ease of creation has raised concerns about intellectual property violations, especially when students print copyrighted or patented designs from online repositories.

photo.alt: A student working on a 3D printed project

stories.title: The role of artificial intelligence in education: Assisted learning or cognitive decline?
stories.summary: AI tools are increasingly influencing students' academic performance and cognitive development, raising concerns about their impact on learning. While some students, like Amir Baig, find AI helpful for personalized learning, educators worry about the potential for reduced critical thinking and academic dishonesty.

photo.alt: Comparison of AI usage in high school students
